**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-12**
**Member:** Reese Iverson
**Member ID:** W871184265
**Reference number:** POC-7908FD6832-14323
**Service denied:** ACL reconstruction, CPT 29888
**Plan:** Passport Health Plan by Molina (Commercial/ACA), Kentucky

---

## A note on the policy and criteria behind this denial

The denial notice I received states that the determination was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria, but it does not identify that policy by name, and no copy of the criteria was provided to me. **Because I have not been given the plan's policy language, I am not quoting any of it in this letter.** I am not going to put words in the plan's mouth or guess at what its thresholds are. Instead, I set out below exactly what is in my medical record, and I ask the plan to measure those facts against its own written criteria — and to send me those criteria, as I request further down.

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of my ACL reconstruction (CPT 29888), which Passport Health Plan by Molina denied on 2026-08-12 under reference number POC-7908FD6832-14323. I am asking for a full reconsideration and for the prior authorization to be approved.

The reason given for the denial was that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I want to address that directly. My understanding is that the packet my surgeon's office submitted contains a documented history, a documented course of conservative treatment, documented medication trials, an MRI, and a physical examination. Below, I have laid out each piece of that record in one place so that nothing is missing from this review. If the plan believes a specific document is still absent, I am asking the plan to tell me in writing which specific document it is, so that it can be supplied rather than the request being denied a second time.

## What my records document

My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, an orthopedic surgeon, has documented that this procedure is needed. The record submitted with the prior authorization request establishes the following:

**Duration and course of symptoms.** I have had nine months of progressive pain in the knee, and it has not been relieved by rest.

**Conservative (non-surgical) treatment, completed and documented.** I completed supervised physical therapy for range of motion and quadriceps strengthening, with bracing, over 14 weeks from 2026-03-17 to 2026-06-23. I completed 16 visits. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.

**Medication trials, completed and documented.** I took NSAIDs for eight months with inadequate relief. I also had a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-25, which gave me only two weeks of partial relief.

**Imaging.** An MRI of the knee on 2026-07-13 shows a complete mid-substance tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with a bone bruise pattern. The menisci are intact and there is no significant arthritis.

**Physical examination.** Examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.

**Functional impact.** I have recurrent instability with pivoting, and my knee has given way twice on stairs.

**Surgical suitability.** I have no active infection and no untreated substance use. My BMI is 29 and I am a non-smoker.

In short: a documented complete ligament tear on MRI, a documented failure of supervised physical therapy, bracing, anti-inflammatory medication and an injection, documented instability with episodes of giving way, and a documented supportive physical examination. That is a complete conservative-care history and a confirmed structural diagnosis, assembled by my treating surgeon. I am asking the plan to review these facts against the criteria it actually applied.

## Request for the criteria used in this denial

I am requesting, in writing, the exact clinical criteria that Passport Health Plan by Molina applied to deny this request. This includes the title of the medical policy relied upon, and the name and edition of any clinical review guideline used. The plan holds these criteria; I do not. I am entitled to them, and I cannot fully respond to a determination whose standard has not been disclosed to me. Please send them to me at the address above.

I am also requesting that the plan identify, specifically, which document or element it considered missing from the submitted packet.

## Closing

I am asking Passport Health Plan by Molina to reconsider this determination and approve prior authorization for ACL reconstruction, CPT 29888. My knee is unstable, it has given way on stairs, and I have already completed months of non-surgical treatment without lasting relief. I would appreciate a written decision that addresses the specific clinical findings above.

I understand my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice — by **2027-02-08** — and I am submitting it within that window. I am sending this appeal to the address printed on my denial letter, which is the authoritative address for this plan. I understand I may also sign in at molinahealthcare.com through the member portal, or call the Member Services number on my ID card, and that Molina is administered on a state-by-state basis. I have confirmed the appeal window against my denial letter, which is authoritative.

Please contact me at the phone number above if anything further is needed. I would rather supply a missing page than have this denied again for the same reason.

Thank you for your time and for a careful review.

Sincerely,

 

_______________________________
Reese Iverson
